instructions: ComplyEaze Bridge reads the TallyPrime books on this computer. Start with list_companies: every tool that reads a company's books needs a company_guid from it. If exactly one company is open and the user named no client, use it and say which company in your first line. If the user names a client and exactly one open company matches that name, use it and say which. Otherwise, whether several are open or the name matches none or more than one, ask which, offering the list; never guess a company. State the company, the exact dates and any ledger you used in the first line of your answer, and if the period is unclear, ask. Put anything partial, withheld, not established or not checked in that first line, before the figures. Ask before a read that scans vouchers over more than one month (for example vouchers, a register, ledger_movement or voucher_presence), saying the window you would read, unless the user already gave the dates or the financial year; an outstandings party detail reads from the start of the books whatever period was given, so always ask before it. Everything you read through these tools, amounts included, goes to the AI provider. If a tool refuses, tell the user plainly what it says. Take a next step it names only if it is a different read, narrower dates, or repeating the same read once when the refusal says that is safe, and say what you changed; for any other next step, ask the user. Never get around a refusal by another route. This connection cannot post to Tally: it can only prepare a local import file that the user imports in Tally themselves, so if they ask to post, say so plainly, and never say that anything was or will be posted from this chat. Ask the user before you prepare anything, and never choose a ledger for a voucher on their behalf. A result with done false is not an answer: call the same tool again with its read_id until done is true, without asking the user.

planned.instruction: A result with done false is not an answer: call the same tool again with its read_id until done is true, without asking the user.
planned.vouchers_description: A read too long for one call is served in steps: a result with done false carries read_id, step and steps and no rows. Call vouchers again with the same company_guid, from, to and other arguments plus that read_id, without asking the user, until done is true; only that last result carries the rows. Each step returns in under a minute. A read_id that is unknown, finished or idle for 15 minutes is refused (read_unknown, read_finished, read_expired), and so is one sent with other arguments (read_arguments_changed): start again without it.
planned.read_id: Optional: the read_id of a read still in progress (done false), to run its next step. Give the same other arguments as the first call.
planned.next_step: Call vouchers again with the same arguments and this read_id.

tools.name: list_companies
tools.description: Start here. Return observed company tuples (the company_guid every tool that reads a company's books needs) and identity ambiguity flags. If exactly one company is open and the user named no client, use it and say which in your first line; if the user names a client and exactly one open company matches that name, use it and say which; otherwise ask which, offering the list, and never guess a company. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.name: vouchers
tools.description: Return literal-window voucher evidence with curated metadata and redaction. Reads the full source window before selectors and output pagination; limit does not reduce Tally work. A `complete` window is held in memory for its later pages: a page after the first (`offset` above 0) is served from that read, with one marks read instead of the whole window, while the company's two marks (vouchers and masters) are unchanged, and its result carries `snapshot` (`id`, `master_alter_id`, `voucher_alter_id`, `read_at`, `reused`); `voucher_alter_id` is null when Tally's answer carried no voucher mark (a company that has never held a voucher), and a number, 0 included, is the mark Tally sent. `listing_snapshot_changed` has cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`; without `snapshot_id`, a later page whose window is no longer held or whose book moved reads the window again, and rows can shift between pages. A `partial` window is not held. A later page is served only for the same question: the same dates (a date is the same however it is written), the same voucher-type selector, search and grouping, and the `ledger` argument exactly as typed on the first page (a differently spelled `ledger` is a different question and reads the whole window again). Without `snapshot_id`, a page whose held window found the book moved reads afresh and carries `earlier_snapshot` (`offsets_do_not_continue` true): start again from offset 0. Only a page whose `snapshot.reused` is true continues the earlier pages: a later page with `reused` false or no `snapshot` is a fresh read whose offsets may not continue them. A change that moves neither mark is not seen; not established: whether a company feature or configuration change that alters export content moves a mark, whether a restored copy of the company with the same marks is told apart, and whether a remote writer's save shows in the marks at once. So a held page can be up to ten minutes old after its read finished; a first page is always read fresh. Use narrow dates; dense windows are unqualified and can fail source limits. `state` is `complete` only when the window's rows were checked voucher for voucher against a count ComplyEaze Bridge made of the window first, or the window was empty, a read widened by a day on each side was also empty, and the company has no vouchers (`reason` `company_has_no_vouchers`); otherwise it is `partial`, with `reason` `nonempty_window_unqualified` when rows were not counted, `empty_uncorroborated` when an empty window's widened read is also empty but the company has vouchers, and `empty_window_wider_read_nonempty` when the widened read found rows on the neighbouring days (the window's own read found nothing and those rows cannot count it, so an empty window beside a busy day cannot reach `complete` today). ComplyEaze Bridge makes that count for every book that has held a voucher, however few, so `nonempty_window_unqualified` is expected only when the company's mark reads zero while the window holds rows. Selectors and the search apply after the window is labelled, so a zero from a `complete` window is a checked zero. A voucher created, altered or deleted between the count and the read refuses with `voucher_window_part_not_admitted`, cause `part_census_mismatch`; call again. Each item carries `cancelled` and `optional` (always booleans; a source that omits or cannot assert either fails the whole read rather than guess). `post_dated`: Tally asserts it on every voucher when the fetch list asks for it, and the key is left out only when a source does not report it, so it is a boolean only when Tally asserted Yes or No. Absent is not evidence of `false`: it means ‘Tally did not say’, not ‘Tally said no’, so branch on key presence, not on falsiness, before treating a voucher as not post-dated. Neither this tool's listing nor `voucher_presence` filters out post-dated (or optional/cancelled) vouchers; the caller decides what a non-posting or unobserved status means for its own computation. (A `summarise_by` call is the exception: it sets aside cancelled, optional and entry-less vouchers and counts them, and sums post-dated ones with a count.) `reference`, `is_invoice` and `party_gstin` follow the same absent-means-not-observed convention as `post_dated`: each key is present only when Tally reported a non-empty value for it, and its absence must not be read as false or as an empty string. `is_invoice` is a boolean exactly like `post_dated`; `reference` and `party_gstin` are non-empty strings when present. A captured book with no GSTIN recorded against a party's ledger has shown `party_gstin` absent on every voucher for that party, which is not evidence Tally cannot report one. Of the voucher-type selectors (at most one of `voucher_class`, `voucher_type_guid` and `voucher_type`), `voucher_class` matches by Tally's own class functions and `voucher_type` ignores ASCII case as Tally does. Voucher-type names are editable in Tally, so a display name that is a class name, or the reserved name of any type in scope, is refused as `voucher_type_ambiguous` whenever the types of that name are not exactly the types of that class or reserving that name; the types involved are listed in `candidates` (bounded to a quarter of the response budget, with `candidates_total` and `candidates_truncated`). Use `voucher_class` or `voucher_type_guid` instead. That check sees only the vouchers in scope: the window read, after any `ledger` filter. A type with no voucher in scope is not seen, and when nothing is in scope nothing is ambiguous. When a `voucher_type` name selects no voucher, one more read lists the book's voucher types: a name no type carries is refused as `unknown_voucher_type`, with the name as `requested` and every type in `candidates`, nearest name first (bounded as above); a name some type carries keeps its zero. A filtered result carries `voucher_types`: the types `included` and every type `in_scope` (name, GUID, own reserved name, class and row count), and each item carries `voucher_type_guid`, `voucher_type_reserved_name` and `voucher_class` (null outside the measured classes). A row whose type Tally cannot resolve, or whose class answers contradict each other or its reserved name, refuses the whole read. A foreign-currency composite (`$1.00 @ ₹ 86/$ = ₹ 86.00`) reads as rupee `amount` plus `foreign` (currency, amount, rate). A voucher that will not read or net to zero is withheld: it passes every date, ledger and type check, then is listed in `withheld_vouchers` (GUID, date, type, number and cause `foreign_currency_amount_unparsed`, up to 100) with an exact `withheld_total`, the same on every page. `items` and `total` then exclude it, `state` is `partial` with `reason` `vouchers_withheld`, and `coverage` says so; the `voucher_types` row counts still include it, and the listing fits a quarter of the response budget. Any other amount Tally did not return as a plain decimal still refuses the whole read, as does a composite whose foreign and base amounts differ in sign while the foreign amount is not zero. `ledger_match` names the ledger read, how (`matched`: `exact`, or `case_or_spacing`, which the answer should mention by naming the ledger read) and any `similar_ledgers` that differ from it only in case or whitespace. Search: `voucher_number`, `reference`, `narration_contains` and `amount` (a plain unsigned decimal, matched against the absolute value of any ledger entry of a voucher, so it finds an invoice total and a tax line alike) keep only the vouchers that satisfy every criterion given. With a search, each item carries `matched` (which criteria held and, for an amount, the positions in `amounts` that equalled it). A blank, over-long or invalid criterion is refused (`search_criterion_empty`, `search_criterion_too_long`, `search_narration_too_short`, `search_amount_invalid`), and a narration phrase is refused as `search_narration_redacted` where narrations are withheld from the assistant. A voucher withheld for a foreign-currency amount is never dropped by an `amount` search, since its amounts cannot be compared: it stays in `withheld_vouchers` and the result stays `partial`. A held window is reused only for the same search, and only for the same listing or summary: a listing and a summary of one question hold separate windows. `voucher_types` counts are taken before the search, so with a search they do not add up to `total`. Summaries (`summarise_by`): Each bucket has `group` (a ledger name, a `YYYY-MM` month, a voucher type name, a group name or a cost centre), `vouchers` (an exact count, each voucher once), `debit` (zero or negative, as `ledger_movement` reports it), `credit`, `net` (debit plus credit) and `voucher_refs` (up to 5 vouchers by date, type, number and GUID; `voucher_refs_complete` says whether that is all of them; a `vouchers` listing without `summarise_by`, narrowed with the existing selectors, lists the rest). Debit and credit follow each entry's sign (a zero amount stays on the side Tally flagged it). A ledger bucket adds the entries on that ledger of the vouchers the window, selectors and search selected: with a `ledger`, type or search given, a counter-ledger's bucket holds only its entries on those vouchers, not that ledger's whole movement. A month or type bucket adds all the entries of its vouchers (debits and credits then equal in size), or only the selected ledger's entries when `ledger` is given. `entries_counted` says which: `all_entries` or `selected_ledger`. A `group` or `primary_group` bucket adds the entries of the ledgers under that group (every entry of the selected vouchers, also when `ledger` is given). A `group` bucket holds only the ledgers directly under that group, as the ledger master shows it (a ledger directly under the root is under `Primary`, with `reserved_name` null), so a predefined group whose ledgers sit in sub-groups has no bucket or a small one: its whole figure, descendants included, is in `subtree_totals` (each group on any bucket's chain with `covers`, `depth`, `vouchers`, `debit`, `credit` and `net` over everything under it, never to be added to a bucket of the same group, whose own `covers` says it holds only the ledgers directly under it, largest movement first, at most 60, with `subtree_totals_total` exact and `subtree_totals_complete`; they overlap, so they do not add up to `totals`). A `group` bucket carries `reserved_name` (empty for a group the book's user made), `chain` (every group from it up to the one under the root, nearest first, each with `name` and `reserved_name`) and `primary_group`. A `primary_group` bucket holds every ledger under the group directly under the root and is keyed by its reserved name, so a renamed predefined group stays one bucket and shows its current name in `group` (a group the book's user made there is keyed by its name). Each has `members` (the ledgers in it with their own `debit` and `credit`, largest movement first, at most 10), `members_total` (exact) and `members_complete`; a group bucket cannot be narrowed with a selector, so trace its vouchers through a member ledger with `ledger`. Group names are shown as the book has them (a group may be named after a party); member ledger names are masked when parties are masked. The groups are the book's masters read now, not the grouping in force on each voucher's date: each ledger's group chain is read before the window and again after it and must be the same, or the call refuses (`group_snapshot_drifted`, or `ledger_snapshot_drifted` if the set of ledgers changed). A ledger that the ledger list does not hold, or whose group chain cannot be walked, refuses the whole summary (`summary_group_unresolved`, with `cause` `no_parent`, `group_absent`, `group_name_repeated`, `reserved_name_missing`, `cycle`, `exhausted`, `top_group_not_under_root` or `ledger_not_in_catalogue`; `ledger` names the ledger that could not be placed, the group is not named, and `no_parent` also covers a parent group Tally returned that ComplyEaze Bridge will not carry). A group summary adds 30 requests to the window read, with or without `ledger`; each call took 64 in one live run; a book of thousands of ledgers was not measured: a book whose master-alteration mark is above 11,983 is refused first (`summary_group_book_too_large`; the limit is provisional and computed, not measured; the mark is an upper bound on ledgers, so a smaller book may be refused), a real book's group buckets may need several pages (use `offset`). Group summaries were checked once, on the live book below: each bucket equalled the ledger buckets added up by the trial balance's own parent column; a large book, a group renamed or moved while a window is read and a held later page were not run live. Each bucket has `position`, its place in the whole ordering (labels of ledgers can read alike when parties are masked, and a masked label cannot be passed back as `ledger`); to list a month bucket's rest, narrow `from` and `to` to that month. `totals` is the debit and credit the buckets add up to, `vouchers_summarised` the vouchers behind them, and `excluded_from_buckets` the cancelled, optional and entry-less vouchers left out (counted, not hidden). Post-dated vouchers are summed, not set aside: `post_dated_included` counts those Tally flagged Yes and `post_dated_flag_absent` those with no flag at all (the read asks for the flag and Tally asserts it on every voucher, so that is expected to be 0; only when it is not does a zero in the first prove nothing); a voucher type that does not post (a memorandum, a reversing journal, a sales or purchase order, a delivery or receipt note), if the book uses it and Tally exports it with ledger entries, is not told apart and is summed too: `basis` says so in the result. Checked once against a live TallyPrime 7.1 on a synthetic book of 67 vouchers (a year, 44 ledgers): every ledger, month and voucher-type bucket equalled the sums over the listed vouchers, the 30 ledger buckets equalled `trial_balance` for the same year, each search returned what the same criterion selects from the listing, and a later page came from the held window in 10 small requests. Not covered: a memorandum, a reversing journal, a voucher withheld for a foreign-currency amount, `mask_parties`, withheld narrations, an item invoice with stock lines, paging of a summary past one page, `ledger` name resolution, another TallyPrime edition or release, Windows, a large book. Cost, from that one run: a plain read took 34 requests, about 7 s and about 6 MB from Tally; each ledger, month or voucher_type summary or search call reads the window again at the same cost, and `ledger` adds 12 requests there, four of them reads of the whole ledger list (a group summary adds 30 with or without `ledger`, below); for a month or more on a large book read ledger totals with `trial_balance` (it has no month or voucher-type grouping and no search; the same year's `trial_balance` took 34 requests and 2.5 s on that book; one day of vouchers took minutes on the largest book measured, a voucher mark of about a million). Bucket `debit`, `credit`, `net` and `totals` are plain decimals with trailing zeros dropped (`1000`, `-87900.5`); an item's `amounts` keep the two places Tally sent (`1000.00`). Withheld vouchers are not in any bucket and the result is `partial`. A voucher whose entries do not balance refuses the whole summary (`voucher_entries_unbalanced`). Buckets are ordered by the larger movement first (ledger, type, group, primary_group, cost_centre), ties in movement keeping the order in which the bucket was first counted in the window, or by month. A held window serves a later page of buckets as it serves a later page of vouchers. Each ledger entry's `bill_allocations` carries `reference`, `bill_type` and `amount`; where Tally sends them it also carries `bill_date` (YYYYMMDD, the original bill's date for an Agst Ref) and `credit_period` (a `value` and a `unit` of days, weeks or months, or `unit` `unrecognised` with its `text` when the text cannot be read); an allocation Tally sent neither for has neither. An entry's `cost_centre_allocations` lists its cost-centre rows as sent (`category`, `cost_centre`, `amount`); an entry without them has no such key (on an item invoice the goods line sits inside the sales or purchase ledger's entry: an allocation list beside it is read like any other, one inside the goods line is flagged as in a shape not recognised, and no captured item invoice carries allocations; category and cost-centre names are trimmed; the amount is as sent; both names are masked under `mask_parties`). The rows are not checked against the entry's amount. On the one book measured with two categories on one entry, each category's rows added up to the whole entry, so do not add rows across categories; `summarise_by: cost_centre` sums them per category and checks each category against its entry. An entry whose list cannot be read whole (a centre with no name or no amount, an amount that is not a decimal, a centre or a category named twice, a category with no name or no centre, a field sent twice, text that cannot be decoded, an empty allocation container, an allocation list in a shape not recognised) carries `cost_centre_allocations_unreadable` with a reason and no partial list, the rest of the response unchanged. A row's `party` is Tally's own PARTYLEDGERNAME for the voucher: on a Receipt, Payment or Contra it can name the bank or cash ledger (on TallyPrime 7.1 it did for a Receipt, a Payment and a Contra that ComplyEaze Bridge imported), so read the counterparty from `amounts`, not from `party`. With `bank_allocations: true` an entry that has a bank allocation carries `bank_allocations` (at most eight; each field a `state` of `absent`, `empty` or `value`, the value trimmed), or `bank_allocations_unreadable` with a reason; an empty `bank_date` is not a sign the entry is unreconciled, and the `reference` search does not look there. A transfer reference typed into a Contra's bank allocation sits in its `instrument_number` on both entries, not in the narration. An entry without it has no such key, which does not mean it has no allocation. With `goods_lines: true` an entry of an invoice voucher that carries goods carries `goods_lines` (at most 1,000): each line's `stock_item`, and its `actual_quantity`, `billed_quantity`, `rate` and `amount` as a `state` of `absent`, `empty` or `value` (the value trimmed, a quantity or rate with its unit, such as `100.000 Kgs` or `25.00/Kgs`), with `batches` (at most 100: `godown`, `batch`, both quantities and `amount`) where Tally split the line; a Purchase line's amount is negative and a Sales line's positive, as the entry's. A line whose batch amounts do not add up to its amount, whose amount is not a decimal or that names no item leaves its entry carrying `goods_lines_unreadable` with a reason and no partial list, the rest of the response unchanged. Item, godown and batch names are masked under `mask_parties`. In the captures Tally sent goods lines under a ledger entry only on invoice vouchers, and the lines of any entry that carries them are shown: a Stock Journal showed none in the one read of it (TallyPrime 7.2, the answer is not committed); a Delivery Note, Receipt Note, Physical Stock and Manufacturing Journal are not captured, and an entry without the key may still have moved stock. Captured on Sales and Purchase invoices of two synthetic books (TallyPrime 7.1, one also on 7.2); not captured: a Credit or Debit Note with items, discounts, additional cost, a bill of materials, a foreign-currency line, a voucher typed on Tally's screen. To ask whether vouchers you mean to post are already in the book, use voucher_presence instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally. A read too long for one call is served in steps: a result with done false carries read_id, step and steps and no rows. Call vouchers again with the same company_guid, from, to and other arguments plus that read_id, without asking the user, until done is true; only that last result carries the rows. Each step returns in under a minute. A read_id that is unknown, finished or idle for 15 minutes is refused (read_unknown, read_finished, read_expired), and so is one sent with other arguments (read_arguments_changed): start again without it.

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

from.description: The first day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: The last day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

voucher_type.description: Optional, at most one of the three: one voucher type's display name, matched ignoring ASCII case. A name that could mean more than one class or type is refused (voucher_type_ambiguous).

voucher_class.description: Optional, at most one of voucher_class, voucher_type_guid and voucher_type: a reserved class, matched however the book has renamed its types, child types included.

voucher_type_guid.description: Optional, at most one of the three: exactly one voucher type, by its GUID. Another company's GUID is refused (voucher_type_guid_foreign).

ledger.description: Optional: only vouchers with an entry on this ledger, spelled as in the book or differing only in ASCII case and spaces. A ledger whose own name differs in case or symbols from the spelling its vouchers carry is reached by either; `ledger_match` shows its own name and, when different, `ledger_row_spelling`, the spelling its vouchers carry.

voucher_number.description: Optional: only vouchers with exactly this voucher number, ignoring ASCII case and surrounding spaces. Numbers repeat across voucher types, so more than one voucher can match.

reference.description: Optional: only vouchers whose reference is exactly this, ignoring ASCII case and surrounding spaces. A voucher with no reference never matches.

narration_contains.description: Optional: only vouchers whose narration contains this phrase (at least 3 characters), ignoring letter case, accent composition and runs of spaces. Refused where narrations are withheld from the assistant.

suspense_tagged.description: Optional, true only, and only together with `ledger` (the suspense ledger): keep the vouchers on that ledger whose narration ends in a suspense tag ComplyEaze Bridge writes ("Bridge: purpose not confirmed; reclassify", or "UNIDENTIFIED - reallocate from" followed by the name of one of the voucher's own ledgers), allowing one trailing [BRIDGE:...] marker after it. Each item says which tag in `matched.suspense_tag`. This classifies by the narration text: it does not prove ComplyEaze Bridge wrote the voucher (the same text typed by hand matches), and a voucher on the ledger whose narration was edited after the tag is NOT listed, so also read the ledger without this filter and treat every voucher left over as still in suspense. Refused without `ledger` (search_suspense_tagged_needs_ledger) and where narrations are withheld from the assistant (search_narration_redacted).

amount.description: Optional: an unsigned decimal such as 1180.50; only vouchers with a ledger entry of exactly this amount (debit or credit). Each item says which entries matched.

summarise_by.description: Optional: ledger, month, voucher_type, group, primary_group or cost_centre. The result then holds buckets of debit, credit and voucher counts instead of the vouchers, over the same window, selectors and search; offset and limit page the buckets. group and primary_group sum each ledger under its group as the book has it now (see the description). cost_centre sums the entries' cost-centre allocations by category and centre; its result's `basis` says how they tie out.

bank_allocations.description: Optional, default false: true adds each ledger entry's bank allocations (bank date, instrument number and date, transaction type, status), each field absent, empty or a value as Tally sent it. Nothing in them says whether an entry is reconciled.

goods_lines.description: Optional, default false: true adds each ledger entry's goods lines on an invoice voucher (stock item, actual and billed quantity, rate and amount, and each godown and batch row), the stock item as a name and each other field absent, empty or a value as Tally sent it; a quantity or rate keeps its unit. A Stock Journal has none here, and no line says its direction: stock_lines reads both. The lines count toward the byte cap of the held page window (64 MiB).

include_e_invoice.description: Optional, default false: true adds e_invoice to each invoice: irn, ack_no and ack_date, each with state present and its value, absent or not_reported.

include_gst_details.description: Optional, default false: true adds each ledger entry's gst_details as sent: taxability and type_of_supply (absent, empty or a value) and rates per duty head (duty_head, valuation_type, rate, per_unit_rate; a rate is absent, empty, zero or a value, never merged). A zero is what Tally sent, not a zero-rated supply: a captured taxed Purchase carried zeros. Not the tax charged (the tax entries' amounts). An item invoice's goods-line rates sit under that line and are not returned. Repeat it on later pages. Unreadable details give gst_details_unreadable with a reason. Also adds voucher_gst (place_of_supply, party_state, registration_type, note_reason, party_note_number, party_note_date) and dispatch (shipping details) to each invoice and any voucher carrying a detail, each stated as in e_invoice.

stock_lines.description: Optional, default false: true returns each voucher's stock_lines, each with direction, item, quantities, rate, amount and batch rows, in place of its ledger entries. Read for Stock Journal, Delivery Note, Receipt Note and Credit Note; other kinds are counted under kinds_not_read. Refused with any argument that needs ledger entries.

offset.description: How many rows to skip before this page: 0, the default, is the first page.

limit.description: Most rows per page; default and maximum 500 unless configured otherwise. A byte limit can end it sooner: continue from next_offset.

snapshot_id.description: Optional, on a later page only: the first page's snapshot_id, so the call is refused (listing_snapshot_changed) rather than continuing from a different read.

read_id.description: Optional: the read_id of a read still in progress (done false), to run its next step. Give the same other arguments as the first call.
